utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about documents, but I assume that it can be found somewhere. But I don't know if there is anything that is archived in that sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's up to the lawyers to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Looking at this document, I cannot help noticing that there are two blank spots. Someone was to be appointed, but there's no indication. And there's to be a deadline, and that is left open. And also I do not see a signature. Did you know this document before you came here to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document I am familiar with from before, because I read the Official Gazette of the Mostar municipality. The document was signed by Jadran Topic personally. It means that it was signed in the original, but then it was just published. It is the R. Vlastrucjno [phoen] and it is standard practice when a document is published in the Official Gazette. At the time, there weren't that many technical possibilities to do things like this. The fact that you cannot see the name or the deadline, well, simply the quantity of the work, the speed, the problems that forced people to do things like this, made them to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, I thank you for answering.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And now for the Trial Chamber and everyone else's note, all of these documents are from the Official Gazette as they were published. If we go to the next document, 1D 0583, this is a decision on a temporary close-down of catering facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What exactly does this mean, and why was it necessary?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC
utterances.text: That was the time of victory. Soldiers were celebrating in cafes. They were armed. In order to establish order, the Municipal Council -- in order to establish order in the town, to prevent drunkenness, they adopted this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, was that both on West and East, or was it just preventing one group of people from drinking and partying, or celebrating, I should say?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC
utterances.text: This applied to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00584. This is a decision to fix the working hours of enterprises in privately-owned stores selling consumer goods, and we see it's restricted from 10.00 a.m. to 1 p.m., 1000 hours to 1300. So could you please tell us, why was this necessary?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC
utterances.text: This is also something that was adopted for the purposes of establishing order in town, so that the shops would not be open all day and that people who worked in the shops also had time to go to the shelters. That is the reason for this decision, to have people stick around for less time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 00586, and we're going to see more of these sorts of decisions. This one is to impose a curfew. This is the first one, dated 30 June 1992, and we see the curfew is from 10.00 until 5.00 a.m., 10.00 p.m. until 5.00 a.m. Could you please tell us why it was necessary to have a curfew at that point in time, and did this apply throughout the city and was it for everyone in Mostar or just for some?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC
utterances.text: This applied for the entire area of the town and applied to all citizens, and the decision was adopted for the purposes of establishing order in the town, since a lot of people were armed and they -- the intention was to prevent these people from moving around town at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Witness, there's going to be a curfew imposed here also, because it's 7.00 p.m. We will stop the hearing now, adjourn. Mr. Karnavas, so far you have used up 2 hours and 35 minutes. Witness, please come back tomorrow for tomorrow's hearing. We are sitting in the morning, so we just have a few hours of sleep in front of us and we will all resume at 9.00, thank you, tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of September, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
